Subject: Notice: ClarifyCloud subprocessor change (VectorOps) — action requested

Hi Vivek,

Quick heads up: ClarifyCloud is onboarding a new downstream processor for our telemetry pipeline — VectorOps, Inc. (Sophia Liu is the primary contact). VectorOps will only process anonymized telemetry and crash logs (no PII). Effective Jan 15, 2027, VectorOps will ingest logs for indexing and query performance analytics.

We are proposing to flow down the existing DPA terms in our MSA to VectorOps and request Redwood's acknowledgement/consent per Section 5.4 of our Order Form. Attached is the updated subprocessor listing (subprocessor-listing-v2.pdf) and a short security summary for VectorOps.

Request: could Redwood confirm by Dec 10 whether (a) the proposed subprocessor is acceptable, and (b) whether you need us to execute a three-party flow-down agreement (ClarifyCloud + VectorOps + Redwood) or if a VectorOps/ClarifyCloud DPA amendment is sufficient.

Link to the proposed redline (live): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-example-redlines

If helpful, Sophia from VectorOps is happy to jump on a 30-min call next week to walk through the controls.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Partner Ops | ClarifyCloud

Thanks Vivek — I reviewed the materials and VectorOps' security sheet. Short summary and recommended next steps: 

Summary:
- VectorOps will handle telemetry and crash logs. No evidence of PII ingestion based on ClarifyCloud's description, but we need an explicit statement (contractual) that no PII is transferred.
- VectorOps provided SOC 2 Type II (latest report attached to the Drive link).

Legal concerns / redline asks:
1) Flow-down scope: Our MSA/Order Form requires that the vendor ensure subprocessors are bound by equivalent DPA obligations. We should ask ClarifyCloud to either:
   a) obtain VectorOps' signature to a DPA flow-down that mirrors our DPA (preferred), or
   b) if ClarifyCloud insists on single-party DPA, require: express representation that VectorOps is bound by equivalent obligations and provide evidence (signed acknowledgement + SOC2 + data handling addendum).
2) Audit / evidence: ClarifyCloud must (i) provide SOC 2 Type II report and (ii) agree to reasonable audit rights limited to audit via third-party assessor with 30 days' notice (we can accept this limited form).
3) Liability carve-outs: avoid unlimited liability transfers. If ClarifyCloud asks VectorOps for indemnity, ensure aggregate caps remain consistent with our MSA.
4) Notice & removal: Require ClarifyCloud to notify Redwood within 10 business days of any change and to remove/replace the subprocessor if it fails controls.

Suggested internal action:
- Ask ClarifyCloud to provide either a three-party flow-down DPA or an executed VectorOps acknowledgement + SOC 2 + standard data handling addendum.
- If ClarifyCloud proposes modifications that increase risk (e.g., no auditable evidence), escalate to me and Vivek for final sign-off.

I attached a redline (redline-msa-vectorops.docx) with specific markups: explicit "subprocessor acknowledgement" paragraph and a limited audit-rights clause (third-party assessor only). If procurement is comfortable with SOC2 + acknowledgement (karthik), we can accept that and avoid a three-party signature.

Please confirm by EOD Dec 9 whether procurement needs a formal PO amendment or additional checklist items. If we need to ask ClarifyCloud for a three-party DPA, I will draft the email and proposed language.

- Neha
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
attachments: redline-msa-vectorops.docx

Hi Vivek / Neha / team,

Thanks for the quick review and the thoughtful redline. We reviewed Neha's requests internally and discussed with VectorOps (Sophia is cc'ed). Proposed compromise below:

1) VectorOps will sign a subprocessor acknowledgement that mirrors the core security/data-use obligations in ClarifyCloud's DPA (we will share the signed form).
2) VectorOps will provide SOC 2 Type II report (we've uploaded to the Drive link).
3) Regarding audit rights — VectorOps is not able to accept direct unlimited audit rights. They will accept a limited third-party assessment process: VectorOps will agree to annual third-party security assessments and will provide assessment reports to Redwood on request; ClarifyCloud will commit to notify Redwood within 10 business days of any material security incident.
4) We are prepared to execute a three-party signature if Redwood requires it, but would prefer VectorOps sign the acknowledgement + SOC2 path to speed onboarding.

Next steps:
- We uploaded the signed VectorOps acknowledgement stub and SOC 2 link to the Drive folder.
- If Redwood agrees to the limited audit approach, we will prepare either (A) a short amendment for VectorOps to sign (we aim to have this signed by Dec 20), or (B) a DocuSign three-party flow-down if you require that. DocuSign link (preview): https://www.docusign.com/ClarifyCloud-VectorOps-Flowdown

Please confirm your preference and we’ll move forward. Happy to set a 30-min call with Sophia if that helps.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Partner Ops | ClarifyCloud
